newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: BTNZ picks GDP growth rising to 4.1 pct by Mar '98.
newsitem.headline: BTNZ picks GDP growth rising to 4.1 pct by Mar '98.

text.p: Bankers Trust New Zealand said on Thursday it expected annual GDP growth to accelerate to 4.1 percent by the March 1998 quarter, from 1.7 percent in the year to March 1997.

"Economic growth has, in our view, started 1997 on a soft not -- past the worst, but initially struggling to accelerate. By mid-1997, however, we think conditions will be more conducive for growth," BTNZ said.

It said the economy would spend the early part of 1997 recovering from the very tight monetary conditions prevailing in 1996, and from uncertainty leading into the election and afterwards during the coalition negotiations.
It saw monetary conditions becoming moderately looser over the first half of the year if activity data retained its soft tone and there was good news on the wages and inflation front.
"In our view the monetary easing cycle will trough sometime between March and June of 1997."
Prospects for the economy were brighter in the second half, however, with the economy starting to feel the effects of the monetary policy easing which began in the December quarter.
In addition, an extra NZ$1.5 billion of government spending (excluding finance costs) in the fiscal 1997/98 year would start to take effect.
"This combination of easier fiscal and monetary policy will move the economy along at a rapid pace during the second half of 1997 and into 1998," BTNZ said.
It said business and consumer confidence would be boosted by a coalition government that had left the economic framework intact, and a stronger world growth outlook should help exports later in 1997.
